findings.title: PHP strcmp() Type Juggling Authentication Bypass
findings.description: The login form uses PHP's strcmp() function to compare passwords. When an array is passed instead of a string (via password[]=test), strcmp() returns NULL which equals 0 in PHP loose comparison, bypassing authentication entirely.

findings.title: PHP strcmp() Type Juggling Authentication Bypass
findings.description: The login form uses PHP's strcmp() function to compare the submitted password with the expected password. By passing the password parameter as an array (password[]=test), strcmp() receives an array instead of a string, causing it to return NULL with a warning. In PHP's loose comparison (== 0), NULL evaluates to 0, which matches the expected return value of strcmp() when strings are equal, thus bypassing authentication.
findings.evidence:
Request: GET /index.php?username=admin&password[]=test
Response: Warning: strcmp() expects parameter 1 to be string, array given in /var/www/html/index.php on line 71
Welcome Admin
Congratulations, here is the flag: flag{5a33e31a-7627-4044-964f-744917d6ca5f}

reproduction.expected: Response contains 'Welcome Admin' and the flag
